article_title: First look: John Lewis and Labrum’s SS26 menswear drop
sub_title: John Lewis and Labrum have teamed up for a second menswear collection for SS26, spanning 35 pieces.
article_content: The 35-piece collection includes denim, tailoring and separates, which will be available online and in five John Lewis stores from 19 March. For the first time, this collection will go beyond apparel, extending into footwear, bags and homeware. Labrum founder Foday Dumbuya said: “This partnership is about the meeting of cultures and craft. Labrum has always told stories through clothing and working with John Lewis has allowed us to expand that language beyond apparel into objects for everyday life. From the Nomoli to Adinkra symbols, each detail reflects heritage, movement and exchange, a reminder that when cultures come together, something beautiful is created.” James Hawkes, head of menswear design at John Lewis, added: “Following the incredible success of our first collaboration, we are so excited to be back with a second collection that truly pushes the boundaries of our partnership. It is particularly thrilling to see pieces from the range debut on the Labrum runway at London Fashion Week, giving our customers a first look at these designs on a global stage a month before they land in-store. We have focused heavily on tactile, bold textures and relaxed silhouettes this season, and expanding into footwear and accessories allows us to offer a cohesive ‘total look’ that our John Lewis x Labrum customers will love.” John Lewis first partnered with Labrum in October last year . The newest collection is described as having a relaxed, casual feel with a focus on texture and detail. Logos and symbols feature heavily throughout, including a bespoke cowry shell jacquard, the classic Nomoli, and meaningful Adinkra symbols which represent West African culture. Prices range from £49 for a 100% cotton T-shirt to £399 for a leather bomber jacket.

article_title: Ex-Coggles buyer readies new store
sub_title: The former head of buying for Coggles at THG, Ryan Haynes, is opening a new independent fashion store in Royal Leamington Spa, Warwick, next month, Drapers can reveal.
article_content: The new 1,000 sq ft store, called Ground, will be weighted towards stocking menswear (70%), alongside a small range of womenswear (30%). Haynes told Drapers this split comes as a result of menswear being “less competitive in the area”. Ground will stock brands such as Wax London, Studio Nicholson, NN 07, Hiking Patrol, Gillian Stevens and Kleman upon opening. Other brands stocked in-store are expected to include Sunflower, Khakis, Pittari, Service Works, Diemme and Stepney Workers Club. Drapers understands the shop will open its doors next month, however an opening date is yet to be confirmed. Haynes recently exited THG following more than nine years as head of buying across Coggles, The Hut.com, My Bag and All Sole. This comes amid a transition period for the Coggles brand, which was sold to Frasers Group in June 2024. Drapers revealed last September that multiple brands stocked at Coggles had their orders cancelled and a number of jobs were understood to be at risk of redundancy amid the transition period. At the time, THG said it was working with Frasers Group to “ensure a smooth handover”.

article_title: David Gandy Wellwear to launch at M&S
sub_title: Marks & Spencer will launch menswear label David Gandy Wellwear on its ‘Brands at M&S’ platform this Spring, in a bid to strengthen its menswear portfolio.
article_content: The launch with Marks & Spencer follows the appointment in February of supermodel Gandy as the first-ever face of Jaeger menswear at M&S . Founded in 2021 by Gandy, the premium lifestyle menswear brand focuses on soft natural fibres with properties such as anti-odour, anti-bacterial and anti-inflammatory and moisturisation. It is sold through his own site and launched at Selfridges in 2022. M&S will offer a wide range of David Gandy Wellwear’s core, best-selling designs including signature, super soft cotton-model T-shirts, comfortable classic cottons and pique polo shirts. Its best-selling range of underwear will also be available, alongside pyjama sets, robes and loungewear. The launch marks a “major milestone” for David Gandy Wellwear, M&S said in a statement, that “reignites Gandy’s partnership with M&S”. The business described Gandy as “a long-time champion of British brands” and “the face of M&S menswear for six years, helping drive sales whilst gaining invaluable personal insight into key aspects of brand building from design, production and marketing.” Gandy said: “From day  one of launch I envisioned M&S as David Gandy Wellwear’s key wholesale partner so this is a big milestone for the brand, and a full circle moment for me given my formative history and recent return to M&S. I love what M&S have been doing recently, and I have experienced first hand the power and impact that M&S has with its loyal, nationwide customer base. “I’m excited that we’re joining its third-party platform to bring David Gandy Wellwear to a much wider audience. We have just recorded three consecutive record-breaking months of sales which is extraordinary in the current retail climate, and I am confident that this new partnership with M&S will accelerate further growth.” Stephanie Macleod, head of brand partnerships at M&S, said: “David Gandy Wellwear is a standout addition to the Brands at M&S platform – a label built on elevated essentials and a unique focus on wellbeing that will really resonate with our customers. “And with David also joining us as the new face of Jaeger, the launch of his brand marks an exciting step forward in our ambition to make M&S the leading destination for modern, quality menswear.”

article_title: Former Matches CCO launches athleisure brand
sub_title: Former Matches chief commercial officer Carl Tallents is launching a new athleisure brand, Now You Live, as he targets growth in the premium activewear market.
article_content: Now You Live will debut online today (17 February) via its direct-to-consumer website, with wholesale distribution to follow at Selfridges , Harrods and Harvey Nichols , supported by pop-up activations. Its debut collection spans gymwear, yoga, pilates and athleisure, alongside knitwear, tailoring, loungewear and accessories. The range also includes the YX 101 sneaker, featuring a Vibram sole and EVA midsole cushioning. Tallents founded the brand after stepping back from corporate fashion to focus on wellbeing and lifestyle, and says he identified a gap for elevated activewear designed to transition from exercise to everyday wear. Now You Live plans to expand into additional performance categories including padel and golf as it builds its presence in the growing athleisure sector. Tallents joined Matches in October 2022 , replacing Elizabeth Von Der Goltz amid an executive shake-up under the leadership of former Asos CEO Nick Beighton. Tallents was previously group head of luxury brands at Frasers Group between 2021-22 and head of brands at the retailer’s luxury arm Flannels from 2017 to 2022. After exiting Matches in January 2024 , following its acqusition by Frasers Group, he went on to serve as chief executive of fashion publications Wonderland and Man About Town.

article_title: M&S names David Gandy as first face of Jaeger menswear
sub_title: Marks & Spencer has appointed supermodel David Gandy as the first-ever face of Jaeger menswear at M&S, marking a significant new chapter for the premium British heritage brand.
article_content: Gandy will front Jaeger menswear across marketing campaigns and digital channels, including M&S Man (@marksandspencerman), the retailer’s dedicated menswear Instagram account launched in August 2025. The channel aims to inspire male customers through styling content and product storytelling, with Jaeger positioned at the premium end of the offer. Gandy previously fronted a dedicated M&S’s Autograph men’s underwear line between 2014 and 2019. Commenting on the partnership, Gandy said: “I’m delighted to be working with M&S again at such a significant moment, as the first face of Jaeger menswear. “Our shared commitment to quality and British style has delivered great success in the past, so I am excited to be working with them on Jaeger – a brand with a remarkable heritage and a modern vision that aligns perfectly with my own approach to menswear.” Gandy’s appointment comes amid strong growth in M&S menswear, driven by a sharpened focus on quality, fit and contemporary design, and underlines the retailer’s strategy to strengthen its premium menswear credentials and deepen engagement with style-conscious male shoppers. Late last year, M&S launched a new menswear collection within its sub-brand Autograph, called Autograph Performance, and in added Hugo Boss to its roster of third-party brands. Jaeger was acquired by M&S in January 2021.

article_title: In pictures: Primark launches 'youth-focused' range
sub_title: Value fashion giant Primark has launched a new "youth-focused" label within its product offering, catering to teenage and young adult Gen Z shoppers.
article_content: The launch of ‘The Primark Scene’ marks Primark ‘s first dedicated youth collection, which has been designed to target the generation of customers who feel “underserved by kids and adult fashion”. Primark’s new label was developed over the past 18 months and “informed by young people”. The range includes outerwear, knitwear, skirts, dresses, tops and shirts, with prices ranging from £3.50 for accessories and T-shirts up to £26 for a boxy hooded jacket. The new collection will be available to shop in dedicated spaces in Primark stores across the UK, Ireland, Spain, Portugal, Italy, France, the Netherlands and the US from this month. Primark chief product officer Steve Lawton told Drapers the initial feedback has been “very positive” and that the launch of the new range is something he is most excited about for 2026. Primark head of buying Kelly-Ann Carroll added: “We’ve spent time listening to young people to understand their world, their lifestyle and what influences their style choices. “The Primark Scene is about giving them the styles that they’re seeing and saving across their social feeds while staying true to what matters to them most: fit, comfort and the best price points. The youth customer excites and inspires our team daily and we want them to feel seen and represented when they shop with us.” Earlier this month, Primark launched its largest ever 240-piece activewear range spanning women’s, men’s and kidswear.

article_title: Primark owner to update on spin-off plan
sub_title: Primark parent company Associated British Foods (ABF) is expected to update on if the potential separation of the fashion retailer from its food business is getting the green light, alongside its interim results, next week (21 April).
article_content: The outcome of a strategic review into the potential demerger of Primark from ABF’s core food business is expected to be detailed in an update to the City on Tuesday (21 April), alongside its latest financial performance. This comes after ABF announced last November it was mulling a possible separation of the Dublin-based fashion retailer. ABF said at the time it was reviewing the separation in consultation with its largest shareholder, Wittington Investments, the investment vehicle of the Weston family, and advisers at Rothschild & Co were appointed to assist with the process in a bid to “maximise long-term value”. Analysts and industry experts speaking to Drapers following the announcement were divided on the implications of a separation of Primark. “A spin-off could unlock value currently hidden within the group, giving Primark greater flexibility and capital to invest in international expansion and digital capabilities,” said Retail Economics head of research Josh Holmes. “ABF’s food business and Primark are also subjected to completely different influences and headwinds, so compartmentalising these areas would be logical,” added GlobalData fashion and apparel analyst Chloe Tedford-Jones. At the time, retail analyst Nick Bubb told Drapers: “I think it would be ironic if, after all these years, ABF decides to separate off its key business, Primark, just as its performance starts to be badly impacted by competition from the Chinese online fast fashion giants.” Drapers has contacted ABF for comment.

article_title: In pictures: Susie Cave launches new demi-couture brand
sub_title: Former model and fashion designer Susie Cave has launched a new demi-couture brand, "Susie Cave, Weddings and Funerals", which will be opening as an appointment-only boutique next month.
article_content: The launch marks Cave’s move away from her brand The Vampire’s Wife, which ceased trading in 2024, and her return to fashion with an experiential shop. The new boutique store will be located at Kensington Church Walk, London, and is expected to open in “mid to late May” this year. Cave described the new store as a location which offers customers a “subtly subversive, surreal and strangely playful atmosphere” to shop. The new range is inspired by theatrical costume wear, rather than traditional bridal or funeral attire, and is described as “ ceremonial and ritualistic”. The initial collection features a range of 25 designs, which can be personalised and custom fit to the client, and will include monotone mini-dresses, as well as elaborate designs, all in black or white. Cave said: “I needed to return to the very basics, to start anew, to shake off the relentless, voracious appetite of the industry and to create beautiful dresses I was personally committed to, beyond the demands of the market.” This follows the official closure of The Vampire’s Wife, which Cave first founded in 2016, on 21 May 2024 with immediate effect following “dramatic implications” of the “upheaval in the wholesale market” at the time.

article_title: Vuori taps former Gap exec for new chief product officer role
sub_title: Californian activewear brand Vuori has appointed former Gap executive Heather Archibald to the newly-created role of chief product officer.
article_content: Archibald, who took on her new position from 6 April, previously served as chief product and merchandising officer at footwear brand Rothy’s (2022-2025). Prior to that, she was chief product officer at activewear brand Title Nine (2021-2022), and was senior vice-president at home furnishings retailer Restoration Hardware (2014-2020). She held positions from assistant merchandiser to divisional merchandise manager at Gap during a 14 year tenure (1999-2013), where she was responsible for the product lifecycle from design to visual display. She has joined Vuori with extensive experience in product leadership, and will lead its global product strategy and innovation. This will include guiding the brand’s investment strategy and shaping its line and assortment architecture. Archibald said in a LinkedIn post: “I’m honoured to announce that I’ve joined one of my all-time favorite brands, Vuori, as chief product officer, along its incredible growth journey. I am looking forward to joining the fantastic team to focus on what I care deeply about – covetable product, customer curiosity, enduring brand vision, and a sustainable purpose.” Vuori founder and CEO Joe Kudla said: “This is an exciting moment for Vuori as we continue to build on our strong momentum and invest in the capabilities that will carry us forward. “With Heather joining the brand, we’re reinforcing our commitment to a product-first approach — deepening innovation, sharpening storytelling and assortments, and bringing even greater rigor to how we scale while maintaining a deep connection with our consumers.” Founded in 2015, Vuori has seen significant growth in the past few years. The brand was valued at $5.5bn (£4.1bn) in 2024, after it secured $825m (£610m) of funding in November 2024 from US based investors General Atlantic, Stripes and others.

article_title: Anthropologie to open store in London’s Coal Drops Yard
sub_title: US fashion retailer Anthropologie is set to open a new store at London's King's Cross shopping destination, Coal Drops Yard, on 6 May.
article_content: The Urbn-owned retailer will take over a 2,300 sq ft retail space that previously housed vintage clothing retailer Beyond Retro. Anthropologie opened its first UK store in 2009, and has since expanded to 20 stores across the country, three of which were opened last year, in Liverpool , Glasgow and Manchester. The new addition to Coal Drops Yard is set to create eight new jobs, and will stock a variety of brands including Anthropologie’s own brands, Maeve and Pilcro, and third-party brands such as Damson Madder, Aligne and Barbour. Managing director Matt Hilgeman said: “We’re excited to open our 21st UK store, in Coal Drops Yard – a highly curated, design-led destination in central London that aligns with our creative, culture-driven community. “We look forward to joining this vibrant retail destination and bringing Anthropologie into a space that feels culturally relevant and creatively inspiring.” The brand added it has plans to host several in-store experiences for customers at its new location. Read more: Meet the team: Anthropologie’s marketing and PR ensemble

article_title: In pictures: Asos takes over Adidas store for new collection
sub_title: The Adidas London flagship store is hosting a pop-up for its third Asos collaboration between 16-21 April.
article_content: The pop-up will be open from 16-21 April, allowing customers to shop the new Adidas Originals and Asos collection . Previously met with sold-out success , Adidas Originals x Asos’ third collection has launched on the Asos app and website, as well at Adidas ‘ London flagship store. The latest 27-piece collection features playful tweaks to Adidas’ classic tracksuit shapes, featuring polka dots and peplums in a selection of neutral, bright blue and pink shades. New styles include a trench coat (£130) and wool knit turtleneck (£40), as well as sportier options such as lace hem sports shorts (£45), and a range of funnel neck zip ups (from £75), which can be purchased with matching tracksuit bottoms (from £65). At the time of the launch, Asos executive vice-president Vanessa Spence said: “Bringing the launch into the Adidas London flagship store alongside Asos.com gives this chapter a new dimension and invites even more people in.”

Debenhams Group has promoted chief commercial officer Richard Vanoli to the role of managing director for online marketplace Debenhams. Footasylum has appointed Gymshark executive Hannah Mercer as CEO, effective from May. Vestiaire Collective has appointed Thomas Hezard as chief product officer and Rémi Bouchez as chief technology officer as the luxury resale business aims to place product and technology at the centre of its next innovation cycle. Mango has appointed Estée Lauder executive Sara Donninelli as chief brand officer, succeeding Blanca Muñiz, who is leaving the business after two years. Asos has named Natasha Jeffers as its new managing director of global trading. Premium Swedish brand Axel Arigato has tapped Adidas veteran Frédéric Serrant for its new CEO, replacing co-founder Albin Johansson. Schuh has appointed Laura King to the role of chief marketing officer with immediate effect. Morgan Fowles, CEO of Tala, the women’s activewear brand founded by Grace Beverley, has left the business. Liberty has appointed Alex Pregnolato, previously chief financial officer and head of transformation at jewellery giant De Beers, to the role of CFO. article_title: Uniqlo snaps up former Ted Baker store
sub_title: Uniqlo has snapped up the former Ted Baker store in Cambridge, with an opening slated for the last quarter of 2026, Drapers can reveal.
article_content: The Uniqlo new store will be located at Unit 33, St Andrew’s Street, Cambridge, following the closure of the Ted Baker store at the location in April 2024. The Japanese high street fashion retailer will also open in Manchester’s Trafford Centre during the autumn/winter period. The Trafford store makes Manchester the first location outside of London to have two Uniqlo stores, following the first opening on Market Street in 2019. Currently operating 24 stores in the UK, Uniqlo opened its first British store in 2001, with its first European flagship opening on Oxford Street in 2007. The news follows the opening of a Bristol location today (16 April), Uniqlo’s first in the south west. Located on the corner of Penn Street and Brigstowe Street in its Cabot Circus shopping precinct, the two-storey 14,640 sq ft store will house Uniqlo’s full “LifeWear” offer across women’s, men’s, kids’ and babies. LifeWear is used to refer to all clothing manufactured by parent company Fast Retailing , which also owns Comptoir des Cotonniers, Helmut Lang and Theory, as well as Japanese brands PLST, Princess Tam Tam and value label Gu. UK COO Alessandro Dudech said: “Opening our Bristol store today is a proud moment for Uniqlo as we continue to grow our presence across the UK. “Bristol’s creativity, culture and strong sense of community make it a natural home for LifeWear. We are excited to finally welcome customers into the space and to become part of the city’s vibrant retail and cultural landscape.” Uniqlo opened in Birmingham’s Bullring in October and upsized its Covent Garden store last month, in response to customer feedback. This feedback directly informed the Fast Retailing -owned business in its decision to double the number of fitting rooms to 32 in the upsized store, introduce baby and kidswear, a dedicated “denim corner”, and reintroduce cash tills to improve access for tourists. The ongoing UK expansion comes amid a record first-half for Fast Retailing in the six months to 28 February, with revenue rising 14.8% year on year to 2 trillion Japanese yen (£9.6bn) and operating profit surging 31.7% to 400.6 billion yen (£1.8bn), propelled by robust global performance at Uniqlo .

article_title: Next CEO pay tops £7.4m
sub_title: Next chief executive Lord Simon Wolfson received a £7.43m pay packet for the year to January 2026, up 51.3% year on year, as strong earnings growth triggered maximum bonus payouts at the fashion retailer.
article_content: Next ‘s latest annual report, published today (16 April), shows Wolfson’s pay rose from £4.91m in the 2024/25 financial year , with the increase largely driven by performance. Fixed pay totalled £1.24m, comprising a £967,000 salary, £48,000 in benefits and a £221,000 pension and salary supplement. Variable pay accounted for £6.19m, including a £1.45m annual bonus and £4.74m from long-term incentive plan (LTIP) awards. The uplift was primarily attributed to strong financial performance during the year: on 26 March, Next reported a 13.4% year-on-year increase in operating profit to £1.24bn for the 52 weeks to 31 January 2026 , as well as a 14.5% surge in profit before tax to £1.16bn. Pre-tax earnings per share rose 17.2% to 990.7p, triggering the maximum annual bonus payout of 150% of salary, while two LTIP awards vested in full after the business ranked second in its peer group for total shareholder return. Across the wider executive team, pay also increased in line with performance, although at lower levels than the chief executive. Next chief financial officer Jonathan Blanchard received £1.59m, while group merchandise and operations director Richard Papp and group sales, marketing and HR director Jane Shields were each paid around £4.7m. Group investments director Jeremy Stakol also received £3.45m. Alongside the remuneration disclosures, Next flagged a more cautious backdrop for international trading, citing disruption linked to the Middle East conflict. International sales growth slowed from 16.5% to 14.3%, with the retailer expecting continued pressure on Middle East sales through the first half. Drapers has reached out to Next for comment. Last month, Wolfson warned that clothing prices could increase by between 4% and 10% if the war in the Middle East persists. The group also said it had increased stockholding by a further 6% to mitigate the risk of supply chain delays, highlighting ongoing uncertainty in global sourcing and logistics. Looking longer term, Next is investing in infrastructure to support future growth, acquiring 84 acres of land next to its Elmsall distribution site. The proposed “Elmsall 4” warehouse, which has planning permission, could add at least 50% more capacity to the complex and support up to £2.5bn in additional sales. Construction could begin by 2028, with phased capacity coming online from 2029, the report added.

article_title: Inditex signs third Lefties store in UK
sub_title: Inditex's value fashion and lifestyle brand Lefties will open in Gateshead's Metrocentre shopping centre this year, marking its third UK store location, Drapers has learned.
article_content: The store will occupy a central unit between Red and Green Mall on Town Square, and marks a North East debut for the brand. In December, Drapers revealed that Inditex had signed two UK stores for its Lefties brand, in Liverpool One and Lakeside shopping centres, set to open in the second half of 2026, when the brand will also launch online. Drapers understands that Liverpool One will be Lefties’ first UK store opening. Lefties currently operates in 18 markets including Spain, Portugal, Italy, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Morocco and Egypt. The new comes after Drapers reported last September that the brand was set to enter the UK market in 2026. At the time, property sources told Drapers that Lefties had earmarked sites of around 50,000 sq ft, including two regional shopping centres, with one of these likely to be in Liverpool. The same sources also said that two of the prospective stores would be in London, however, these were unlikely to be central due to size restrictions, which Inditex has since confirmed. Headquartered outside Barcelona, Lefties is the last of the Inditex brands to enter the UK market, following Zara , Pull & Bear , Bershka , Stradivarius , Massimo Dutti , Oysho and Zara Home. Originally launched in 1999 as an outlet for off-price, leftover Zara stock, Lefties has since developed into a standalone concept that includes a women’s, men’s and kidswear offer, as well as homeware, launching its first collection more than 10 years ago. Women’s cotton T-shirts are priced from €2.99 (£2.62), jeans from €12.99 (£11.38), blazers from €19.99 (£17.52) and dresses are priced up to €29.99 (£26.29). The openings follow “robust” performance at the Spanish retail conglomerate, which reported sales growth of 3.2% to €39.9bn (£34.5bn) for the year to 31 January 2026 , as well as a 3.9% surge in gross profit to €23.2bn (£20.7bn). Ben Cox, Director at Sovereign Centros from CBRE, Metrocentre asset managers, said: “We’re proud to confirm that Lefties are the latest exciting new entrant to commit to Metrocentre. As one of the first Lefties stores in the UK, this is another major endorsement of Metrocentre as a key location for international brands investing in UK retail. “Lefties’ trend-savvy offer will be a compelling addition to our retail mix, and this signing, once again, reflects the dominance and appeal of our scheme to both national and international retailers. With our consistent footfall, extensive catchment, and quality retail offer, we continue to stand out as the leading destination in the region.”

article_title: UK economy inches up in February
sub_title: The UK economy grew by 0.5% in February according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), trouncing City forecasts of 0.1%.
article_content: Services and production both climbed 0.5%, and construction grew by 1% in February. Manufacturing grew 1.2%. However, the manufacturing of textiles, wearing apparel and leather goods was down 0.12% during the month. The wholesale and retail trade (which includes motor repairs) was up 1.4%, “driven by a growth of 3.1% in wholesale trade, except motor vehicles and motorcycles”. The ONS has also revised January GDP to show 0.1% growth rather than the previously published stasis. Earlier this week, however, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), slashed its forecast for UK growth in 2026 from 1.3% to 0.8% as the Middle East conflict weighs on prosperity, with rising fuel prices, borrowing costs and dented consumer confidence. Companies including Hermès , LVMH and Tesco have all warned on the weight of the conflict on business, and fashion and textile suppliers have warned that while rising raw material costs are yet to fully filter through to retail, price increases across the clothing supply chain are inevitable.

article_title: Primark powers on with Middle East store openings
sub_title: Value fashion giant Primark is powering on with its store expansion in the Middle East, despite ongoing conflict in the region.
article_content: Primark opened the doors to its first store in Dubai on Thursday 26 March, located in Dubai Mall, marking its first store in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and second in the Middle East , following its opening in Kuwait last October. The new 60,000 sq ft flagship store, opened in partnership with franchise operator Alshaya Group , spans one sales floor and has created 600 new jobs in the region. The opening in Dubai Mall was followed by Primark’s second store opening in Dubai at City Centre Mirdif shopping centre last week (9 April). The 35,000 sq ft store is also set across one floor and will create more than 300 new roles. A third Dubai-based store, located at the Mall of Emirates, is planned for later this spring, with further openings in Bahrain and Qatar also expected later this year. A Primark spokesperson told Drapers: “ While our entry to Dubai was planned for many months, our decision to proceed was made with careful consideration of the current situation. “The safety of customers and colleagues always comes first. We have been working closely with our partner, Alshaya Group, and are being guided by their local expertise as well as official guidance in the region. “Day-to-day life there continues, with retail and hospitality remaining open and we are committed to supporting customers in Dubai today and into the future.” Primark’s ongoing store expansion in the Middle East comes amid escalating conflict in the region since US-Israeli strikes on Iran began on 28 February. Fashion retailers have since told Drapers they face heightened uncertainty as they tackle sky-high oil prices, shipping disruption and stock delays, while suppliers are warning that rising raw material costs, which are yet to filter through to retail, are likely to cause price hikes.

article_title: Tesco F&F sales top £1.2bn as retailer warns on Middle East
sub_title: Sales of Tesco's F&F clothing line climbed 5.1% year on year to £1.2bn for the year ended 28 February 2026.
article_content: The supermarket attributed this to a strong performance in its activewear range and more premium “Edit” range, which includes a 100% cotton poplin shirt for £18 and wide-leg linen trousers for £25. F&F also relaunched online during the year, as exclusively revealed by Drapers,  increasing access to customers across the UK. Overall sales at Tesco  (excluding fuel) rose 4.6% during the year to £66.58bn, compared with the year prior. Adjusted operating profit crept up 0.8% to £3.15bn for the year. Tesco increased the width of its guidance to reflect the uncertainty caused by the Middle East conflict. The business predicted adjusted operating profit of between £3bn and £3.3bn for the 2026/27 financial year, but said that “much will depend upon the duration of the conflict and in particular, the potential implications for UK households and the economy more broadly”. Following the 5.1% pay rise for Tesco staff announced in March, CEO Ken Murphy announced a £65m “special performance award for colleagues in our stores, distribution centres and customer engagement centres” in today’s results. Murphy said: “We are committed to doing whatever we can to help keep down the cost of the weekly shop, and with the conflict in the Middle East creating further uncertainty for consumers and the economy more broadly, that commitment matters more than ever. “Over the last year, despite cost pressures from new regulation, we have increased our investments in keeping prices low, further improving quality and offering even better service. Customers are choosing to shop more with us as a result, leading to our highest market share for over a decade. Our investments have been made possible by our Save to Invest programme, which has delivered over £2.2bn of savings over the last four years, funding lower prices for customers and higher pay for colleagues, including our recent 5.1% increase in UK hourly pay.”

article_title: In pictures: John Lewis launches second Rejina Pyo collection
sub_title: Inspired by looks from 1990s stars including Julia Roberts, John Lewis's second collection with Rejina Pyo includes slip dresses and soft tailoring. First John Lewis has launched a second collaboration with designer Rejina Pyo, debuting 1990s-inspired styles for spring/summer 26.
article_content: Inspired by looks from 1990s stars including Julia Roberts, John Lewis ‘s second collection with Rejina Pyo includes slip dresses and soft tailoring. First launched in October 2025, the collaboration brings back previous popular items including a mixed stripe cotton shirt (£119), which features a cinched waist, alongside takes on Rejina Pyo’s signature oversized collars, reinterpreted in the contrast stitch detail shirt (£129). The familiar buckle feature returns in the footwear and bags categories with new colourways – strappy kitten heels (£109); s atin buckle flat mules in cornflower blue (£119); while the previous season’s buckle bag returns in a new slouchy hobo shape featuring brown suede (£159) and baby blue leather (£169) options. Designer Rejina Pyo said: “For this second collection with John Lewis the 1990s became a reference point, not in a literal way, but in its attitude: a quiet strength, a simplicity in how pieces are worn and lived in. “I wanted to explore a sense of ease and natural confidence, something that feels instinctive rather than overworked.” Rachel Morgans, John Lewis fashion director said:“We love collaborating with Rejina and her team, blending our creative styles and passion for quality to create something new and exciting for our audiences. “My stand out this season is the tailoring, it will last in your wardrobe season after season and you can wear it in multiple ways. It’s the perfect way to add colour to your wardrobe without sacrificing sophistication.” The collection is available for purchase online and in five John Lewis stores.

article_title: Middle East conflict dents sales at Hermès
sub_title: Middle East sales at Hermès were down 5.9% year on year to €160m (£139m) in the first quarter ended 31 March 2026, at constant exchange rates.
article_content: This was down 13.4% on a reported basis. Hermès said that sales declined slightly at current exchange rates due to significant negative impact of currency fluctuations of €290m (£252.1m). The figure was “significantly impacted by recent geopolitical developments in the region from March onwards”, largely affected by sales in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain. Total group sales rose 5.6% to €4.1bn at constant exchange rates, down 1.4% on a reported basis. The French luxury house also recorded a 2.8% decline in sales (on both constant exchange and reported basis) to €347m (£301.76m) at home, similarly impacted by a decline in Middle Eastern tourists visiting France in March. European sales (excluding France) climbed 9.7% to €538m (£467.6m) thanks to local demand. This was up 7.6% on a reported basis. The Americas region soared 17% to €739m (£642.3m), with balanced growth across the US, Canada and South America, up 6% on a reported basis. Asia Pacific sales (excluding Japan) underwent modest 2% growth to €1.9bn (£1.65bn). This was down 3.9% on a reported basis. Japanese sales also rose 9.6% to a €404m (£351.1m) during the quarter, also thanks to native shoppers. This was a 3.9% decline on a reported basis. By sector, Hermès’ primary category of leather goods and saddlery climbed 9% on a constant exchange basis due to new and updated handbag silhouettes, ready-to-wear and accessories eked up 0.4%, silk and textiles (which houses its iconic scarves) and was up 8% “driven by continually renewed creativity across both the women’s and men’s collections”. Despite the “economic, geopolitical and monetary uncertainties around the world”, the maison confirmed its “ambitious goal for revenue growth at constant exchange rates”. Last year, the luxury group surpassed luxury rival LVMH , becoming the most valuable luxury company by market capitalisation for the first time. In October, it was announced that British designer Grace Wales Bonner would take over from Véronique Nichanian as creative director. Axel Dumas, executive chairman of Hermès, commented: “In a tense geopolitical environment, Hermès maintains its course, true to its long-term strategy. Supported by its abundant creativity, its uncompromising quality and the loyalty of its clients, Hermès is continuing its profitable growth in 2026 with confidence and conviction. The fundamentals of the Hermès model are more than ever a differentiating strength.”

article_title: Puma appoints former Adidas exec to lead creative direction
sub_title: German sportswear brand Puma has appointed former Adidas executive James Carnes to the newly-created role of senior vice-president of creative direction.
article_content: Carnes has joined to lead the brand’s creative direction, innovation, and product excellence, reporting directly to Puma chief brand officer Maria Valdes, with immediate effect. He previously worked at Adidas for 19 years, where he held his first creative director position between 2004-2008. During his time there, Carnes held senior leadership positions where he implemented creative direction across its global design studios, executed celebrity collaborations and business strategy. He served as vice-president of global brand strategy and sustainability of Adidas for six years (2015-21); before joining UK based brand Pangaia as a strategy consultant (2021-23). Since Carnes left Adidas, he has founded two footwear brands Coalition Footwear and Chpt3, and worked as an independent brand strategy and development consultant. Puma chief brand officer Maria Valdes said: “James is a very highly regarded leader in our industry and he has been instrumental in shaping some of the most influential performance and lifestyle products, labels, and platforms. “With a strong background in industrial design and a deep understanding of both athletes and consumers, he will play an important role in getting our customers and consumers excited about Puma once again.” He said of his appointment: “Creative direction is about more than seasonal trends and colours. It is about defining how Puma holistically presents itself in the market, harnessing the company’s portfolio of world class innovation, and deeply connecting with consumers. “We have the amazing opportunity to modernize the image and style of one of the most iconic sports brands in the world and I look forward to leading our teams and collaborating with my colleagues to make this happen.”

article_title: Ann Summers cuts staff safety incidents by 42% after body camera trial
sub_title: Ann Summers has reported a 42% reduction in staff safety incidents following an eight-week trial of body-worn cameras, with plans to roll out the technology across additional high-risk stores.
article_content: The trial, conducted in Ann Summers ‘ flagship locations on Oxford Street in London, Edinburgh’s Princes Street and Nottingham city centre, also led to improved staff confidence and in-store behaviour. The Edinburgh store recorded no police-attended incidents during the period, including during the busy Fringe annual comedy festival season, which runs every August. Ann Summers body-worn cameras Ann Summers introduced the cameras in response to rising levels of aggression and abuse towards shopfloor staff, reflecting a broader industry trend. According to the British Retail Consortium , there are more than 1,600 incidents of violence and abuse against retail workers each day in the UK. Ann Summers said the trial demonstrated that body-worn cameras can act as an effective deterrent without negatively impacting the customer experience, with no complaints recorded during the test period. Head of business risk Sam Tenner said the move was aimed at improving staff safety amid growing challenges on the high street, with incidents involving aggression, intimidation and substance use becoming more common: “It’s a sad fact that it’s tougher to work on our high streets, and with resources dwindling, the ability for police to respond in the way in which we might hope isn’t realistic anymore. “Our motivation was purely around making our people feel we’re investing in the right tools to keep them safe and showing them how to use those tools to actually de-escalate aggressive behaviour,” he added. The retailer is using camera technology from Reveal Media , alongside its digital evidence management system, which allows footage to be securely stored and reviewed when required. Following the trial, Ann Summers told Drapers in November it would expand the rollout to 23 additional stores identified as higher risk, as part of wider efforts to improve employee safety and retention.

article_title: Alohas branches into bags
sub_title: Barcelona-based footwear brand Alohas has expanded its product offer with the launch of its first bag drop.
article_content: The Hilma bag joins the brand’s accessories collection, with ten variations across maxi, midi and mini sizes, launching at the end of May. Described as a “platform for individuality”, the bag is designed for customisation and personality – with a transparent front pocket to slip in a personal note, photograph or keepsake, and metal side rings to hold charms or keychains. Prices range from £245 for a mini to £395 for a maxi, and will be available both online and in stores across Barcelona, Madrid, Milan, Amsterdam, Paris, London, Copenhagen, New York, and Los Angeles. The brand opened the doors to its first standalone sore in London’s Soho last August. Alohas products are designed in Barcelona and produced in Spain, Portugal and Cambodia. Emmelie Karlstrom, head of design footwear, bags and accessories at Alohas, said: “Hilma introduces a distinctive wavy construction, creating a soft architectural profile that feels both modern and effortless. “Rather than concealing belongings, Hilma invites them into view, turning the bag into a subtle narrative of its owner’s personality.” Operating on an “on demand” model, Alohas prides itself on prioritising sustainability by producing without surplus. The brand uses a pre-order system to forecast demand ahead of production. Online, its products are launched at a 30% discount to encourage customers to shop “on demand”. As production begins, its products are sold at 15% discount, and while in stock, the product is sold at full price and can be received within 24-48 hours.

article_title: First look: Maebe's new ‘Between Seasons’ collection
sub_title: Molly-Mae Hague’s womenswear brand Maebe has announced it is launching a new trans-seasonal collection, "Between Seasons".
article_content: The 31-piece edit aims to reflect the “realities of modern British dressing” through its use of layering and an array of versatile yet polished pieces. The new collection is designed to complement Maebe’s consistent offering of elevated staples and dependable pieces, with each piece being developed through expanded wear-testing and enhanced production processes. Launching this week on Maebe’s website, retail prices range from £40 for a halter vest top to £130 for a cotton twill jacket with removable neck scarf. The collection aims to celebrate “dressing with intention”, the brand said, with pieces that are designed to be versatile enough for wearers’ varying situations, from work to parenthood.

article_title: M&S announces updates to Sparks loyalty programme
sub_title: Marks and Spencer has relaunched its Sparks loyalty programme, replacing points with cash rewards as it looks to drive customer spend and support its digital growth strategy.
article_content: The updated scheme introduces a digital “Sparks wallet”, allowing M&S customers to earn monetary rewards that can be spent across food, fashion, home and beauty. The move follows customer feedback calling for a simpler rewards structure and greater transparency. The programme is powered by expanded use of data and artificial intelligence ( AI) , with M&S using machine learning to tailor offers based on shopping behaviour. Further generative AI capabilities are expected to be introduced to increase personalisation over time. Customers can earn rewards through targeted spend-based offers, product bundles and incentives to shop across different categories they had not explored bef0re. A new in-app Sparks hub will centralise personalised offers and rewards. Examples of spend-based M&S Sparks rewards include: M&S has also launched its first external partnership, linking Sparks with Virgin’s rewards platform to allow customers to earn additional rewards on travel and services, including up to £130 when booking a Virgin Atlantic Holiday. M&S chief executive Stuart Machin said: “Customers told us they want Sparks to be simple, rewarding and personalised, and we listened. “New Sparks is built around a much more personalised experience, no tricksy pricing and real money rewards to thank our customers for shopping with us.” The relaunch forms part of M&S’s wider investment in digital and data capabilities, with the retailer positioning Sparks as a key tool to increase frequency, basket size and customer loyalty.

article_title: Topshop launches capsule collection with Tolu Coker
sub_title: Topshop has announced a capsule collection with British-Nigerian designer and multidisciplinary artist Tolu Coker, with a collection preview unveiled during London Fashion Week yesterday (19 February).
article_content: The 18-piece collection comprises knitwear, blazers, pleated trousers, and jumpsuits, all designed with a focus on longevity. The collection also explores different tailoring and construction techniques, with the aim of “transeasonal versatility”. Coker, who was a finalist for the 2025 LVMH prize, is recognised for her narrative-led approach to design. The collection’s pieces were all crafted in line with Topshop ’s circular design criteria, focusing on durability and utilisation of recycled materials. Select pieces from the collaborative capsule collection were given a first look by London Fashion Week attendees yesterday, including King Charles III, Little Simz, Stella McCartney, and Laura Weir . Knitwear pieces appeared alongside Coker’s mainline collection during her runway. Michelle Wilson , managing director at Topshop, said: “The reaction to the runway reveal shows just how significant Tolu’s creative voice is. This collaboration reflects everything Topshop stands for today, championing individuality, creativity and cultural relevance. “Working with Tolu has been incredibly inspiring, and the collection represents a shared belief in fashion as a platform for storytelling. We are proud to support her vision and bring something so considered, expressive and meaningful to our global community.” Tolu Coker said of the collection: “Topshop was my first job when I was 16, so this collaboration is personal, but it’s also a statement of intent. We designed with restraint, maintained quality, considered quantities, and circular choices, because accessibility shouldn’t mean excess. “The collection is built to live beyond a season: transeasonal, versatile, and made with longevity in mind. I believe the positive future of our industry lies in collaboration.” The full capsule collection will be available for purchase globally online at Topshop from early March.

article_title: First look: Tess Daly's Naia Beach launches activewear
sub_title: Luxury swimwear brand and Drapers Independents Awards 2024 winner Naia Beach, co-founded by TV presenter Tess Daly and Gayle Lawton, has expanded its offering with an activewear range.
article_content: Naia Active is a capsule of activewear pieces, comprised of two ranges: the Everyday Soft-Line collection and the Day-Luxe collection. These ranges include leggings, vests, sweatshirts and joggers, featuring signature details such as gold accents and zips. Retail prices range from £30 for a baseball cap to £105 for a bomber jacket. Daly said: “Naia Active is a natural extension of our beloved brand. Our community has consistently told us how much they value our fit, attention to detail and our thoughtful approach to designing for women, by women. This collection is a continuation of that – a celebration of the female form. As we like to say, the Naia woman is every woman.” Naia Beach is well known for its wide range of luxury swimwear and resortwear which features sculpting details anddx is stocked in the UK by John Lewis. Lawton added: “This collection [activewear] is an expansion of who the Naia woman is. Like our swim, every piece has been fitted multiple times across different body shapes, sizes to ensure our signature fit. As women, we know how activewear should feel. Creating pieces so comfortable you forget you’re wearing them and want to keep them on all day long was essential.” Naia Active will officially launch online at naiabeach.com at 6pm today (7 January). Read more: Drapers Independents Awards 2024 winner: Tess Daly’s Naia Beach

article_title: Asos adds Noughts & Kisses to brand portfolio
sub_title: Asos will add Liverpool-based womenswear brand Noughts & Kisses to its extensive brand portfolio later this year, Drapers can reveal.
article_content: Noughts & Kisses is set to launch at Asos at the end of the first quarter of the year, debuting with a 30-piece collection for the spring season. Noughts & Kisses told Drapers the first collection launching on Asos has been curated to “represent the full Noughts & Kisses aesthetic” and includes a range of its signature styles across tailoring, occasionwear and premium basics. A selection of the range will be exclusively available to shop online at Asos as part of the collaboration. Noughts & Kisses founder Jemma Bramley said the brand’s customer “aligns closely” with Asos’ customer base, with a focus on “trend conscious and value clothing”. “Asos is the perfect next step for us because it expands our reach while still preserving the independent, boutique feel we are known for,” said Bramley. “The platform celebrates emerging talent and premium design, both of which sit at the core of Noughts & Kisses.” Noughts & Kisses was first founded in 2011 and retail prices range from £15 for earrings to £150 for a vegan leather jacket. Noughts & Kisses will join the likes of existing Asos third-party brands including Nike , Arket, Mango and recent addition Arrange.

article_title: First look: Ganni x Barbour SS26
sub_title: Ganni and Barbour have unveiled their fourth collaboration for the pre SS26 season, featuring classic wax jackets, quilted coats and a small capsule of accessories.
article_content: The limited edition range, which launched on 4 December, introduces new peplum silhouettes that nod to the shape of the Ganni x Barbour 2024 Re-Loved jacket, which was originally created for Barbour’s Quilting exhibition that marked the 30th anniversary of the brand’s Liddesdale quilted jacket. In addition, Ganni’s recognisable leopard print returns, featuring on jackets alongside Barbour’s tartan print. It also features a capsule collection of accessories including a tartan waxed tote bag, 100% wool beret hat and a lambswool scarf. Items can be purchased online via Ganni and Barbour websites, where retail prices range from £125 for a wool beret hat to £600 for a hooded wax anorak. The two brands first collaborated in November 2022, when the duo launched a collection of Re-Loved and ready-to-wear items. Barbour’s Re-Loved is its programme to give old, pre-owned waxed jackets a new life through hand restoration or upcycling.

article_title: First look: Primark unveils second collection with Perrie Sian
sub_title: Value fashion giant Primark has unveiled its second curated collection with influencer and Reasn co-founder Perrie Sian for spring/summer 26.
article_content: Perrie Sian ‘s second collection of “Perrie’s Primark picks” follows her first collection with Primark for the autumn/winter season in November last year, which saw Primark record its biggest ever day of click-and-collect since its launch. The new spring/summer collection is centred around denim and tailored pieces, including a range of tall and petite leg lengths following “popular demand”. Prices range from £5 for a cotton boxy white T-shirt to £34 for a pink suede blazer. The new season collection launches today (3 February), and is available to shop in-store and online via Primark ‘s click-and-collect service. Sian said of the collection: “I am so proud to be back in Primark stores across the UK for our spring drop. To see how people reacted to the first Perrie’s Primark Picks was beyond my wildest dreams, and to have that collection achieve Primark’s highest click-and-collect website sales was the cherry on top. “It was a huge indication that my audience was ready for this partnership to come to life after years of organically promoting the brand. This Perrie’s Primark Picks has a strong denim focus and I have to be bold and say I think this is THE best denim that Primark has ever done. “It washes so well and I’m really excited to see both tall and petite leg lengths introduced.” The fashion influencer and Reasn co-founder, which she launched alongside In The Style founder Adam Frisby , was also formerly creative director at In The Style under Frisby’s leadership.

article_title: Paul Costelloe: a designer with 'exceptional technique and unwavering passion'
sub_title: Respected Irish fashion designer Paul Costelloe died on 22 November aged 80, surrounded by his wife and seven children. Costelloe was personal designer to
article_content: Respected Irish fashion designer Paul Costelloe died on 22 November aged 80, surrounded by his wife and seven children. Costelloe was personal designer to Diana, Princess of Wales from 1983 until her death in 1997, and is the only designer to present at every London Fashion Week since its launch in 1984. Former managing director of clothing and home at Marks & Spencer, Richard Price said: “An incredible man much loved by all that knew him.” “His creativity never ceased to amaze those who came to his shows,” added Simon Berwin, former managing director of men’s tailoring supplier Berwin & Berwin and owner of his eponymous menswear advisory firm. Born in Dublin in 1945, Costelloe went on to study at the Grafton Academy of Fashion Design before moving to Paris to study haute couture. He launched his eponymous label, Paul Costelloe Collections, in 1979, and presented collections in Paris, Milan and New York, as well as at London Fashion Week. “Paul Costelloe will be remembered for achieving incredible longevity in a fickle industry – and for a hard-working rigour that was tangible in his remarkable output,” echoed Emily Gordon-Smith, trends and foresight director at Stylus. Both a fashion designer and a keen painter, Costelloe also cycled almost everywhere, a hobby he continued well into his 70s. He drew much of his design inspiration from cycling through London’s Knightsbridge. Berwin first met Costelloe in Shanghai around 2oo6. “He had been painting by the riverside, which was his real passion,” he told Drapers. The pair discussed the possibility of launching Paul Costelloe menswear together, which soon came into fruition via a tailoring offer, before being extended into a full menswear range. Berwin & Berwin held the licence for Paul Costelloe for 15 years. “There are not many designers who are able to cross over from women’s to men’s,” Berwin added. “One of the very best – a gentleman who understood the integrity of designing truly beautiful clothes,” commented Barbara Horspool , former chief product officer at The White Company and founder of loungewear brand Mamu. Paul Costelloe spring/summer 26 “Costelloe’s work was a reminder of what fashion once stood for: rigorous training, exceptional technique, and an unwavering passion poured into every garment,” commented Karen Collier, founder and director of her eponymous executive search firm. “These values feel increasingly rare today, which makes his loss even more profound.” Julia Aitken, owner of independent boutique Stanwells in Lymington, Hampshire, described Costelloe as a “gentleman” and “a true Irishman whose heritage ran through his collections”. Costelloe famously collaborated with Irish department store chain Dunnes Stores for the Paul Costelloe Living Studio collection, a partnership which began over two decades ago. He was also the closing designer for the first edition of Ireland Fashion Week in October this year. In a statement, the Irish department store chain said: “Dunnes Stores is deeply saddened with the passing of Paul Costelloe. For over 20 years, Paul brought his unique vision, energy and creativity to our collaboration, leaving a lasting impression on our customers and colleagues alike. We extend our deepest condolences to Paul’s family during this difficult time.” Costelloe remained at the core of his brand throughout his career. “[Costelloe] was so active and lively, and was still going to all the fabric and garment shows,” adds Berwin. A popular figure, there was a line of attendees waiting to speak to Costelloe at his autumn/winter 25 show in February, where he told Drapers that he would have liked more support from retailers in the wider UK market. “He was a truly commercial visionary,” continues Gordon-Smith, “stretching his brand name to incorporate successful licenses and collaborations, playing to his strength (classic, timeless design) and not over-pandering to seasonal trends.” “His collaboration with Dunnes is different, [but] I’ve never understood why a UK retailer never backed him properly,” said Berwin. “His taste levels and love of fabric and colour were so special.” The Paul Costelloe brand will continue under steerage from his son William and daughter Jessica. Jordi Vall i Saborit will continue in his post of head of design, which he has held since 2013, As to whether Costelloe’s eponymous label will change direction following the designer’s death, Berwin thinks this unlikely. “Jordi will ensure continuity, and William has been learning from his father. So the brand will continue as is. It may even grow.” As well as his unquestionable impact on the British fashion industry, anyone sharing thoughts about the late designer also commented on his charm and kindness. “Paul was tremendous fun with a charm and sense of humour that one doesn’t forget,” said Stylus’s Gordon-Smith. “He was also a real family man, and it makes total sense that his children will become the proud custodians of his future brand legacy.” Aitken describes “many happy memories of his shows at London Fashion Week, and also with us hosting charity trunk shows at Stanwells. Great fun, great talent and never a dull moment when with Paul.” Beyond his craft, Paul was known as a genuinely lovely person. “Warm, humble, and committed to nurturing the next generation,” according to Collier. “The industry will deeply miss his presence, his standards, and the heritage he carried with such grace.”

article_title: SLA the Label founder Sarah Ashcroft to launch Oh Polly collection
sub_title: SLA The Label founder Sarah Ashcroft has joined forces with Scottish womenswear etailer Oh Polly to create new collections for the brand.
article_content: Unveiling the news on Instagram, Ashcroft said that Oh Polly had approached her to create her own collections for the brand, and the first one was dropping in November. She wrote: “As you all know bringing designs to life has and always will be a passion of mine and something I have missed incredibly, so working alongside the team at Oh Polly to create my own collections feels like the perfect fit. My first collection is dropping in November, and I cannot wait to share it with you all.” A post shared by SARAH ASHCROFT (@sarahhashcroft) Ashcroft closed her independent London-based womenswear brand, SLA the Label , in February this year. At the time she said on Instagram that the decision was the result of a long-running problem with manufacturing. She continued: “It is with an incredibly heavy heart that I share the news that, after six years of dedication, passion and relentless hard work, SLA has come to an end. This is not a post I ever imagined having to make, and the heartbreak of letting go of something I have poured my everything into is truly beyond words.”

article_title: Net-a-Porter launches exclusive Victoria Beckham capsule
sub_title: Net-a-Porter has today (9 October) launched an exclusive capsule collection with Victoria Beckham.

article_title: First look: Arne opens first store
sub_title: Warrington-based clothing and footwear brand Arne opened its first ever standalone store at Liverpool One shopping centre on 13 September.
article_content: Over the last three years, Arne has launched two successful pop-up stores as well as an interactive event, which allowed the brand’s most loyal customers to meet its founders and gain exclusive early access to product. Located on Peters Lane, the 6,750 sq ft flagship houses “fan-favourite” pieces from across men’s and womenswear, as well as Arne Bites, an in-store ice cream shop and bakery. Steel walls, mirrors and marble reflect the brand’s clean aesthetic. Founded in 2018 by brothers Reece and Ryan Broadhurst, Arne’s mission to create “affordable luxury” has resonated with consumers: operating profits for the year to 29 December 2024 more than doubled year on year, from £4.7m to £11.3m, up 142%. Turnover also hiked 123%, from £37.5m to £84.1m. Read more: Why Liverpool is a northern fashion retail powerhouse Rob Deacon, asset management director at Liverpool One, under Landsec, said: “Arne’s first ever standalone store reflects a longstanding and successful partnership between Liverpool One and the brand. “The latest in a series of digital native brands to commit to Liverpool One, Arne’s permanent store is emblematic of the demand from innovative global retailers looking to capitalise on our second-to-none city centre location, high footfall, and leading reputation.” Ryan and Reece Broadhurst added: “It means so much to us to have finally secured the perfect location, in the only city we ever imagined opening our first physical store. “We wanted to bring something to Liverpool that’s never been done before: a store fit-out of this level, calculated down to the pound per square foot, while keeping our product prices accessible. “Our goal is simple, to [offer] more value than ever before and deliver one of the best shopping experiences, all whilst having a good chance at being able to afford the products inside the store.”

article_title: First look: Jewellery brand Tutti launches womenswear collection
sub_title: Jewellery brand Tutti, led by former Whistles MD Helen Williamson, has launched its first womenswear collection.
article_content: The collection, named “The Edit”, includes a selection of tailoring, textured knitwear, shirting, as well as a chocolate suede jacket and drawstring bag. It is exclusively available in Tutti’s concept store in Harbour House, a creative space in North Shields, Tyne-and-Wear. The launch closely follows Tutti’s rebrand and Williamson’s appointment as fractional managing director in August. Tutti founder Kate Rose worked closely with designer Amy Whitfield on the collection. Each piece uses high quality fabrics, such as cashmere, wool and pure cotton in neutral shades including white, camel and navy. Rose said: “The Edit is all about accessible luxury and effortless dressing. I wanted to create a capsule collection that the modern Tutti woman could wear on repeat all the way from Monday morning to Sunday markets, with beautiful pieces that make dressing the easiest part of the day. “I’m thrilled to see our concept store open its doors and can’t wait to be able to let our customers experience our first fashion collection for themselves.” Williamson said: “The launch of Tutti’s first womenswear collection is such a pivotal moment for the brand and I’m so proud to be part of this journey. What busy, modern women want from fashion brands has evolved and our collections reflect that, with effortless everyday pieces, designed for life and curated for ease. “I loved Kate’s idea for a concept store, and seeing this brought to life in North Shields has been incredibly inspiring. The store provides opportunities for all the Tutti team to engage with our customers in person and receive direct feedback on pieces within the collection, which is invaluable to us as we look to the future.”

article_title: Victoria Beckham sales and profits rise
sub_title: Premium womenswear business Victoria Beckham saw total revenues climb 26% to £112.7m in the full year to 31 December 2024, marking the fourth consecutive year of double-digit revenue growth for the former Spice Girl's eponymous brand.
article_content: Victoria Beckham’s EBITDA was up 22% from £1.8m in the previous year to £2.2m. EBITDA excluding the fragrance business, which was launched at the end of 2023, grew 47% year on year. Fashion sales at Victoria Beckham were driven by midi and gown-style crêpe dresses in bold colourways. The business also relaunched denim, grew its leather goods offering, and unveiled a collaboration with Spanish high street retailer Mango during the period. Direct-to-consumer sales through the brand’s London flagship store in Mayfair and ecommerce website rose 26% year on year, accounting for 62% of total net sales. Victoria Beckham now plans to expand its wholesale portfolio by adding more than 130 new stockists globally by the end of 2025, bringing its total to 200. The business also aims to gain wider exposure this autumn with the launch of a Netflix docuseries following Beckham’s SS25 Paris Fashion Week show and exploring her journey since launching the brand. Victoria Beckham CEO Sybille Darricarrère Lunel , formerly of Dior, Galeries Lafayette and The Kooples, who was appointed to her current role in July, said: “2024 was a pivotal year for the Victoria Beckham business, marked by strategic investment and rightsizing to position the business for long-term, profitable growth. “Despite a challenging market environment, the company delivered its fourth consecutive year of double-digit revenue growth, underpinned by strong consumer demand and continued brand momentum across both fashion and beauty.”

article_title: First look: Paul Smith and Barbour join forces for new collection
sub_title: Paul Smith and Barbour have launched a 23-piece collection, 'Paul Smith Loves Barbour', today (1 October).
article_content: The new launch reimagines a selection of Barbour ‘s most iconic coats, and includes knitwear, accessories and T-shirts. Inspired by country shows, the collection plays upon country classics via “unusual” shades of waxed cotton, patchwork pieces and a Friesian cow motif. Both brands have brought their recognisable aesthetic and British heritage to the collection, with Barbour representing the British countryside and Paul Smith’s city life design. As well as the marriage of town and country, the collaboration combines tradition with modernity to create a collection that is “unexpected, and full of personality”. Pieces include chunky knitwear using speckled yarns, waxed jackets and bucket hats, rain boots and enamel pin badges. Ian Bergin, Barbour director of menswear, footwear and accessories, said: “There is always a certain wit that Sir Paul [Smith] brings to the table which shines through in this collaboration. Beautiful garments, hidden touches and a playfulness in execution which melds with Barbour’s practicality and style. The final result is a collection which genuinely feels like an authentic meeting of brands, with both Paul Smith and Barbour’s quintessential spirits very present and visible throughout the pieces. We are excited to see it launch.” Barbour operating profits jumped to £39.5m for the year to 30 April 2024, up from £34.3m the year prior, which the Tyneside-based business attributed to successfully implemented cost reductions and gains in foreign exchange rates. However, turnover dipped 6% year on year from last year’s “record” £343m to £322m amid a “challenging” wholesale environment and rising costs. Paul Smith reported a widened pre-tax loss of £5.3m for the 12 months to 30 June 2024, compared with a loss of £2.3m the previous year, due to “a lack of consumer confidence”. Turnover at Paul Smith dropped 7% year on year to £197.8m, driven by a 13% decline in wholesale revenue. The business attributed the falling sales to “a lack of consumer confidence in major markets”, including the UK, Germany, Italy and France.

article_title: RETAIL 2011
sub_title: There isn’t a more dynamic industry in the UK than retailing, and the UK retail scene is constantly changing. It makes the need for timely information and
article_content: There isn’t a more dynamic industry in the UK than retailing, and the UK retail scene is constantly changing. It makes the need for timely information and understanding of where the retail economy is at more important than ever.  This report is designed to give a rounded picture of exactly where UK retail is as we enter 2011. For this report, Retail Week interviewed 25 chief executives and board directors from major UK retailers, representing the full spectrum of categories. We asked them for their views on the economy, the outlook for consumer spending, on their business and their plans to expand. We went into more detail on areas for investment, notably multichannel and technology, and areas that represent a particular challenge in 2011, like supply chain. We combined the insight from the interviews with the depth of understanding built up by Retail Week and in particular our information service Retail Week Knowledge Bank, and combined that with research pulled together from the most authoritative sources covering the sector to create what we think is the comprehensive guide to retailing in the UK in 2011. article_title: John Lewis onboards more than 100 brands to bolster fashion offer
sub_title: John Lewis has onboarded over 100 fashion brands so far this year, including Vivienne Westwood and an exclusive Paul Smith collection, as it bolsters its fashion offer to stay competitive with rivals Marks & Spencer and Next.
article_content: This includes London-based designer Rejina Pyo , launching on 9 October, following its successful collaboration with British luxury brand Awake Mode . Both collaborations came to fruition via the retailer’s partnership with the British Fashion Council. John Lewis has added new brands across all categories including womenswear, menswear and kidswear, spanning clothing, footwear and accessories. Notable new brands include JS John Smedley, Sessun and Second Female in clothing, as well as Alohas and an exclusive 25-piece Mulberry collection across its footwear and accessories business. Read more: Peter Ruis bets big on fashion at John Lewis: ‘The sky’s the limit’ Rachel Morgans, director of fashion for John Lewis, said: “In retail you’ve got to ask, ‘What’s going to make customers cross the road to us?’ Our fashion and beauty offer is key to this, which is why we’re carefully curating a premium quality range that offers customers something different. “When it comes to brands, we’re not chasing numbers, but focusing on those that appeal to our customers and offer something new. By mixing big hitting premium options, like Vivienne Westwood, with soon-to-be favourites and upcoming names from the industry, we’ve got a really exciting mix and we’re backing British talent. “Exclusives play into this too, and we’ve some brilliant ones in the pipeline including a 25-piece collection with Mulberry. This comes alongside wider investment – both in our stores and our customer offer – such a huge revamp of our beauty halls, and new brands like Rihanna’s Fenty Beauty.”

article_title: Bershka opens Manchester flagship with augmented reality
sub_title: Fashion retailer Bershka has opened a flagship store at Manchester's Trafford Centre, featuring augmented reality technology.
article_content: Spanning 12,917 sq ft, the store is divided into three standalone zones, each dedicated to one of the Intidex retailer’s main lines: Bershka, BSK and Man. The design concept attempts to align the interior with the brand’s global store format, already used in various locations worldwide. The layout features a series of modular display units to present each collection, with varying materials and finishes between sections to differentiate them. Each area is accessible through its own entrance and furniture is used to visually separate the spaces. A muted grey palette creates a neutral backdrop for the clothing. The checkout areas have been designed as sculptural wooden installations, incorporating both traditional staffed and self-service tills. Lighting throughout the store has been custom designed for this flagship, using compact rectangular LED spotlights that cast a warm, welcoming glow. Bespoke acoustic panels have also been installed in the central spaces of each zone to enhance the auditory experience. The store’s facade uses textured stone in an effort to make it stand out within the shopping centre. Read more: First look: Zara brings new high-tech store concept to UK Bershka has also introduced augmented reality mirrors, offering an interactive experience for visitors. The mirrors allow shoppers to virtually try on items using exclusive filters developed by the brand. By scanning a QR code, customers can access Bershka’s digital fitting room via the app, where they can test different filters and share their looks on social media. The AR mirrors are available only at the Trafford store for a limited time and were developed in collaboration with creative tech studio Ffface.me and social media platform Snapchat. The retailer prioritised eco-friendly materials, lighting systems and construction methods throughout the creation of the store. As part of the Bershka Music Project, the brand has partnered with the independent radio station NTS, which will act as music curator for the store, focusing on emerging talent. NTS will produce playlists and in-store sets to soundtrack the shopping experience, while also creating unique musical activations for Bershka locations. To celebrate the launch, NTS hosted a live broadcast of the reopening on its digital platform, supported by a pop-up radio station created exclusively for the event.
